newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Aid groups airlift staff from Sierra Leone town.
newsitem.headline: Aid groups airlift staff from Sierra Leone town.

text.p: U.N. and other relief groups airlifted foreign staff from Sierra Leone's second town of Bo on Wednesday after fighting broke out there between Kamajos traditional hunters and soldiers, aid workers said.

A chartered plane and helicopter left the embattled town with about 30 international workers on board, they added. A couple of foreign aid workers remained in the town after failing to make the rendezvous with the plane.

Security has been a major problem in Bo since Revolutionary United Front rebels took up arms in 1991. Its population, which includes civilians fleeing rebel and other attacks in the bush, is now 250,000 -- three times the pre-war figure.

Military officials said rivalry between the army and the Kamajos, who act as vigilantes to protect their own and other property from rebels, flared on Tuesday when soldiers tried to arrest a Kamajo who shot a civilian caught stealing.
Kamajos attacked army bases in Bo on Wednesday, they said.
Military officials in Freetown said a number of soldiers, Kamajos and civilians had been killed in the fighting.

The rebels and the army agreed a ceasefire before the-then military leader Julius Maada Bio restored civilian rule in March. Civilian President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah and rebel leader Foday Sankoh extended the truce indefinitely in April.
A spate of attacks blamed on rebels have put the ceasefire under strain but neither side has spoken of returning to all-out war. R
